properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Anthony, 2026-08-11: "there have several times where I've forked off somebody's repo and tried something just to see if it was possible... do we allow users of reflow2 to 'fork' off a main design and explore without having the requirement for anything they build to have 'requirement' linked to it. then if the exploratory fork off main design works, is there a way to 'merge' into main?" His own lean, recorded as his: "can something merge into main design without a requirement associated with it (I'm kind of leaning towards no)".

⭐ THE QUESTION SHARPENS TO ONE THING: WHERE THE GATE SITS. Nobody is proposing that unmotivated work be invisible — `unmotivated_capability` fires today and should. The open question is whether it should be SILENT IN A FORK and BINDING AT THE MERGE, which is a different placement, not a different rule.

⚠️ THE COST OF THE CURRENT PLACEMENT IS MEASURED, and it is in `dec:exploratory-staging`: a Capability at `planned` with no Requirement raises THREE gaps — `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability`, `unverified_capability` — "THREE GAPS EACH, FOREVER, BY CONSTRUCTION". On 2026-08-10 that was 34 of 73 open gaps, 47% of the list, from backlog rows that were wishes nobody had agreed to. An exploratory fork is the same shape at speed: every spike accrues three gaps, and a fork built to answer "is this even possible" would be all noise by the end of an afternoon.

📌 SO THE FORK CASE MAY BE THE MISSING EVIDENCE `dec:exploratory-staging` IS WAITING FOR. That decision's closing question is "DOES A NOT-YET-AGREED WISH BELONG IN THE DESIGN AT ALL?" and its options (b) a `proposed` Capability status and (c) route wishes to a Decision are both about giving unagreed work a silent home. A fork is a place where unagreed work is not merely tolerated but is THE POINT, which is a stronger argument for a silent home than a backlog row ever was. These should be read together.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) GATE AT THE MERGE, NOT THE WRITE. The fork writes freely; `apply_merge` refuses to land a Capability with no incoming SATISFIES unless the merger states one or explicitly accepts it as unmotivated. This is EXACTLY the shape `apply_merge` already has — `dec:merge-three-way` makes it refuse, writing nothing, until every conflict is decided — so the mechanism is a second refusal reason rather than a new mechanism. It also matches Anthony's lean.
(b) SILENCE THE DETECTORS IN A FORK by marking the design exploratory, so gaps stay quiet until it is merged. Cheap, and it hides real findings: a fork that is quietly incoherent looks identical to one that is fine, which is the false-green class this project keeps finding.
(c) DO NOTHING. Explore in a fork, tolerate the gap noise, and let the merge be an ordinary merge. Zero build cost; the noise is the cost, and it is the cost `dec:exploratory-staging` already measured at 47% of a real gap list.
(d) REQUIRE MOTIVATION AT THE WRITE EVEN IN A FORK — the status quo. Honest and it forbids the thing Anthony is describing: you cannot try something to see if it is possible if you must first say why you want it.

⚠️ THE ARGUMENT FOR HIS LEAN, stated because it is stronger than it first looks. What lands in the primary design becomes what the golden thread computes delivery from. `req:completion-computed` (accepted) derives delivery FROM the thread rather than from a status field, so a Capability merged in with nothing behind it silently degrades the one number the design is supposed to be able to state honestly. A fork can afford incoherence because nothing computes from it; the primary design cannot.

⚠️ THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IT, equally real. `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (proposed) exists because a body of intent that contradicts itself is still a design, and `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` says the target is a consumer's project — where brownfield reality is that things get built and the requirement is written afterwards, if ever. A merge gate that admits no unmotivated work forbids adopting the very case `adopt` exists for. Whatever is chosen must let a merger say "yes, this is unmotivated, and I am taking it anyway" and have that recorded rather than blocked — which is what makes (a) a two-sided accept and not a wall.

⚠️ AND THE HONEST WARNING FROM THE SAME FAMILY: the detect-and-ask skill forbids inventing a requirement to close `unmotivated_capability` — "a requirement backed out of the thing that implements it is satisfied by construction and can never contradict anything." A merge gate that demands a requirement will produce exactly those unless the accept-it-anyway route is first-class and cheap.
properties.name: OPEN — may an exploratory fork build without requirements, and is the motivation gate at the WRITE or at the MERGE?
properties.rationale: The question is not whether unmotivated work is visible but where the gate sits. Gating at the merge lets a fork do what a fork is for while keeping the primary design's delivery number honest, and it reuses apply_merge's existing refuse-until-decided shape rather than inventing one. The fork case is also stronger evidence for dec:exploratory-staging's open question than the backlog rows that raised it, since in a fork unagreed work is the point rather than a leftover.
